summary: Backend logging and OpenTelemetry bootstrap shared by Clash Node services (api-node, render-server) and Cloudflare Workers (api-cf). Instrumented code depends on @opentelemetry/api only; this package is the pipeline edge.
context_hints: Log lines use the product-wide LogRecord envelope from @clash/shared-runtime/logging, one JSON line per record, plus an OpenTelemetry Logs API emit (no-op until a provider is registered).

Node services start the official NodeSDK before application code with `node --import <bootstrap>`; export follows the SDK's standard OTEL_* environment behaviour, except that an otlp exporter needs an explicit endpoint: with no OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (or signal-specific ..._{TRACES,METRICS,LOGS}_ENDPOINT) that signal is off, and with no signal on the SDK is not started. OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true turns it off regardless.

Workers do not run the Node SDK: the cloudflare adapter maps @opentelemetry/api onto native `cloudflare:workers` tracing so shared-code spans nest under platform spans; export is configured in wrangler [observability].
Spans and logs carry ids, counts and durations; never prompts, credentials or user content.

key_files.src/log.ts: createServerLogger: LogRecord JSON line to console (with active trace/span ids) + OTel Logs API emit.
key_files.src/cloudflare.ts: WorkersTracerProvider / installWorkersTracing: OTel Tracer over native Workers custom spans; status -> otel.status_code attributes, no span ids yet (platform limitation).
key_files.src/node.ts: resolveNodeTelemetrySignals: which signals the environment enables (endpoint required for otlp). startNodeTelemetry: NodeSDK with http, undici, pg and runtime-node instrumentations, ESM loader hook via module.register; default service.name overridable by OTEL_SERVICE_NAME.
key_files.src/node.test.ts: Signal resolution and SDK start/no-start per environment (mocked NodeSDK), plus subprocess smoke tests: --import bootstrap really instruments ES-module node:http and fetch, and logs carry the server span's trace id.
